movie_title: How the world’s tallest skyscraper was built - Alex Gendler
introduction: Discover the engineering innovations that made building Burj Khalifa, the world’s tallest skyscraper

vocabulary.definition: cause to seem small or insignificant in comparison
vocabulary.example: The new skyscraper in Dubai was designed to dwarf all other buildings in height.

vocabulary.definition: actions taken to prevent or counteract a harmful situation or condition
vocabulary.example: The architects implemented various countermeasures to ensure the tall skyscraper could withstand strong winds.

vocabulary.definition: able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions
vocabulary.example: The building's exoskeleton design made it more resilient to wind forces.

vocabulary.definition: a rigid external covering for the body in some invertebrate animals, providing support and protection
vocabulary.example: The skyscraper's innovative exoskeleton design helped distribute weight and resist wind pressure.

vocabulary.definition: supported or reinforced by a projecting structure
vocabulary.example: The buttressed core of the Tower Palace III in South Korea provided additional support to the building.

vocabulary.definition: to an astonishingly great or surprising degree
vocabulary.example: The Burj Khalifa was completed in a staggeringly short five-year period considering its immense height.
